explain.say: On the grid, electricity must be made at the very moment it is used, because the wires store almost nothing. If supply and demand drift apart even slightly, the grid's frequency starts to change.

faq.q: Why must supply match demand exactly?
faq.a: The grid has almost no storage of its own, so every watt used must be generated at the same moment. Too little supply makes the frequency fall and too much makes it rise, and big swings can cause blackouts.
asks: What happens if supply and demand do not match?

faq.q: Why do sun and wind make the grid harder to run?
faq.a: Their output depends on the weather and the time of day, not on how much people need. Grid operators must fill the gaps quickly with other power stations, imports or storage.

faq.q: How long can a grid battery run?
faq.a: Most grid batteries are built to deliver full power for 1 to 4 hours. Longer gaps, like a calm, dark week in winter, need other storage such as pumped hydro or hydrogen.
asks: How much energy does a battery farm store?

faq.q: How do batteries help keep the grid stable?
faq.a: They watch the grid frequency and push power in or soak it up within a fraction of a second, long before a power station could react. This service is called frequency response.

faq.q: How big are grid battery farms?
faq.a: Large ones are made of hundreds of container-sized units and can store hundreds or even thousands of megawatt-hours, enough to supply a city for a few hours.
asks: What does a battery farm look like?

facts: Most grid-scale batteries are designed to deliver full power for between 1 and 4 hours.
Grid batteries can respond to a change in grid frequency in under a second.

quiz.say: What do grid batteries mostly do with spare solar power at midday?

options.show: Store it to release in the evening
options.say: Store it to release in the evening

quiz.why: They charge while solar power is plentiful and discharge in the evening peak when the sun has set.

wrong.1: Batteries store electricity chemically; they do not make natural gas.
wrong.2: Wasting the power as heat is exactly what storage avoids.
